newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ascom shares surge after Nexion sale.
newsitem.headline: Ascom shares surge after Nexion sale.

text.p: Shares in Swiss telecommunications group Ascom Holding gained sharply on the Swiss Exchange after the company announced the sales price for its loss-making Nexion unit.
At 0930 GMT Ascom bearer shares were up 90 Swiss francs, or 5.9 percent, at 1,610 francs. In early trading the shares had hit a new year high of 1,630 francs.
Ascom had already announced the sale of Nexion in April, but neither the buyer nor the selling price.
Earlier today Ascom said it had sold Nexion to a U.S. subsidiary of Fujitsu Ltd for a gross sum of $130 million, minus transaction costs.
The transaction costs cover fees for lawyers and banks and the dissolution of Nexion's stock option plan, Swiss News Agency SDA quoted an Ascom spokesman as saying.
The spokesman said these transaction costs amounted to between 15 or 20 percent of the sales amount or between $19.5 and $26 million.

Nexion is a development company that employed some 180 people, mainly engineers. It has no revenue, but in the first half of 1996 Ascom's Enterprise Networks division, which grouped Nexion and the Timeplex units, reported a loss of 39 million francs.
